direct_prompt: Abstract:We present the development of a new, three-dimensional, Lagrangian magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) code called MAGMA (MHD Applications using a Godunov Method and Adaptive mesh refinement). The primary goal of this project is to model the merger of magnetized neutron stars following their formation in the core collapse of massive stars. Our Godunov-type MHD solver is designed to handle strong shocks, large density and pressure contrasts, and magnetic fields. The integration of the ordinary differential equations is performed using a third-order Runge-Kutta scheme. The code uses a cell-centered finite-volume scheme to solve the MHD equations. The spatial reconstruction of the variables is based on the piecewise parabolic method (PPM). Adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) is used to locally increase the resolution where needed, reducing the computational cost. We describe the numerical methods employed, and discuss the results of a number of one-, two-, and three-dimensional tests. The one- and two-dimensional tests include shock tube problems, the collapse of a magnetized cylinder, the Sedov blast wave, and the Parker instability. These results demonstrate that the code performs well and is capable of accurately capturing the dynamics of MHD flows. Three-dimensional tests of the AMR algorithm are also presented, and we show that significant computational savings can be achieved by using AMR for problems with large spatial dynamic range.

title: Matrix Exponential-Based Closures for the Turbulent Subgrid-Scale Stress  Tensor
direct_prompt: Here is a 6 sentence abstract for the provided article title:Accurately modeling the subgrid-scale stress (SGS) tensor is crucial for large eddy simulation (LES) of turbulent flows. Traditional eddy viscosity models make overly simplifying assumptions that limit their applicability. This paper presents a new class of matrix exponential-based SGS models to address these issues. The models are derived by applying the matrix exponential to SGS tensor evolution equations, yielding tensorial closures without an isotropic assumption. Numerical results show that the new models capture important anisotropic behaviors absent from classic eddy viscosity closures. By relaxing common assumptions while maintaining computational efficiency, the proposed matrix exponential closures improve LES predictions of problems involving complex turbulent flow physics.

These closures account for the dynamics of the velocity gradient tensor and overcome limitations of other models. However, existing closures require specification of an empirical decorrelation time scale that limits their applicability at high Reynolds numbers. In this paper, we explore improvements to matrix exponential closures through numerical experiments and analytical considerations. We examine the effects of using time-correlated stochastic forcing instead of white noise forcing and perform expansions of the matrix exponentials in powers of the decorrelation time scale. The results provide insights into the stability of closures as a function of the velocity gradient invariant and ways to potentially extend the applicability of these models to higher Reynolds numbers.

Drawing from theoretical developments in continuum mechanics and recent studies applying matrix exponential functions to characterize material nonlinearities, we develop a closure formulation where the subgrid stress tensor is expressed as the matrix exponential of the rate-of-strain tensor multiplied by a coefficient tensor that depends on filter-scale quantities. title: A Radio Nebula Surrounding the Ultra-luminous X-ray Source in NGC 5408
direct_prompt: **Abstract:**The nature of the compact radio source associated with the ultra-luminous X-ray source (ULX) in the nearby galaxy NGC 5408 is investigated using multi-frequency radio observations, including new Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) 1.5-GHz data. The source is clearly resolved with an extent of ~30 kpc, indicating a radio nebula rather than a compact jet. A spectral index map of the radio nebula shows a steepening of the spectrum from the center to the outer region, which can be explained by energy losses of relativistic electrons in the nebula via synchrotron radiation and inverse Compton scattering of cosmic microwave background photons. The energetics and timescales involved suggest that the radio nebula is most likely formed via the reprocessing of an earlier short-duration enhanced mass-loss event from the luminous blue variable (LBV) star associated with the ULX, rather than a continuous wind.

A common approach to solving CSPs is to use a local search algorithm, which iteratively modifies a given solution until a solution satisfying all constraints is found. A key challenge in designing a local search algorithm for CSPs is to decide which variables to modify at each iteration. A promising approach is to freeze some of the variables and only modify the remaining variables. However, it is not known how to choose the variables to freeze in order to maximize the efficiency of the local search algorithm. In this paper, we propose a new method for freezing variables in random CSPs. Our method is based on the idea of identifying the variables that are most likely to be involved in conflicts during the search process. We show that our method can significantly improve the efficiency of local search algorithms for solving random CSPs.

We analyze the empirical relations between rotation period and stellar age, and investigate the effects of stellar mass, metallicity, and binarity on these relations. We find that gyrochronology can provide accurate ages for main-sequence stars, but its accuracy decreases for more evolved stars. The method is limited by the uncertainty in stellar radii, rotation rates, and age determinations. Furthermore, the assumption of a constant angular momentum evolution does not hold for all stars, leading to systematic errors. title: Multiwavelength Study of X-ray Selected Star Forming Galaxies within the  Chandra Deep Field South
direct_prompt: Abstract:The multiwavelength properties of a sample of 144 X-ray-selected star-forming galaxies in the Chandra Deep Field South are studied using a variety of ancillary multiwavelength data, including deep optical and near-infrared imaging, ultraviolet (UV) and mid-infrared photometry, and optical spectroscopy. The median redshift of the sample is z = 0.94. The galaxies span a range of UV and X-ray luminosities, stellar masses, and star formation rates. The UV-to-X-ray spectral slopes of the sample galaxies are found to be correlated with their X-ray luminosities. The X-ray properties of the sample galaxies are compared to those of optically selected star-forming galaxies at similar redshifts. The X-ray luminosities of the X-ray-selected sample are found to be systematically higher than those of the optically selected sample, at a given UV luminosity or stellar mass. The differences in X-ray properties between the two samples are likely due to differences in their star formation histories. The X-ray-selected sample galaxies have higher specific star formation rates and younger stellar populations than the optically selected sample galaxies. These results suggest that X-ray selection is biased toward galaxies with ongoing starbursts.

No significant excess of events is observed above the expected background, and limits are set on the oscillation parameters. These limits are the most stringent to date from a collider experiment, and they provide new constraints on models of neutrino oscillations.

title: Link concordance, homology cobordism, and Hirzebruch-type defects from  iterated p-covers
direct_prompt: Here is a 5 sentence abstract for the provided academic article title:This paper investigates topological properties of iterated p-covers, a construction in which a manifold is mapped onto itself multiple times in a way determined by a prime number p. Specifically, the authors examine notions of link concordance and homology cobordism for these constructions. They demonstrate that links and homology spheres arising from iterated p-covers satisfy additional concordance and cobordism relations beyond the classical definitions. Furthermore, numerical invariants generalizing the classical Hirzebruch signature defect are defined for iterated p-covers. The behavior of these new Hirzebruch-type defects is studied, yielding insights into topological invariants of the construction.
prompt_few_shot: Here is a 5 sentence abstract for the given academic article title:This paper studies the properties of link concordance and homology cobordism groups through the use of invariants arising from iterated p-covers. Iterated p-covers of links and 3-manifolds are constructed, and Hirzebruch-type defects are defined from the covers to obtain homomorphisms from the link concordance and homology cobordism groups to algebraic structures. The kernels of these homomorphisms are investigated, and applications include results about the structure of the Cochran-Orr-Teichner filtration of the knot concordance group. Examples of independent slice links and 3-manifolds are constructed through the use of these new covering invariants and their associated defects.
prompt_SICO: Here is a 5 sentence academic abstract in human writing style based on the given title:This paper examines the relationships between link concordance, homology cobordism, and Hirzebruch-type defects that arise in iterated p-cover constructions. By studying the behavior of iterated cyclic p-covers of branched covers of S^3 along links, we identify topological invariants that characterize cobordism classes of homology spheres and link concordance classes. In particular, we show how certain defects, generalizing the classical Hirzebruch defect of simple branch covers, account for changes in Rohlin's μ-invariant and the Kirby-Melvin invariant under such constructions. Furthermore, these defects can be packaged together to give homology cobordism invariants of the corresponding iterated branched covers. The relationships elucidated provide new perspectives relating knot and homology 3-sphere concordance to properties of iterated cyclic branched covers and their relative defects.

title: Une plate-forme dynamique pour l'\'evaluation des performances des bases  de donn\'ees \`a objets
direct_prompt: Voici un résumé en 12 phrases pour l'article "Une plate-forme dynamique pour l'\'evaluation des performances des bases de donn\'ees à objets":Les bases de données à objets sont de plus en plus utilisées pour leurs capacités à gérer des données complexes. Cependant, il existe peu d'outils pour évaluer leurs performances. Cet article présente une plate-forme dynamique conçue pour répondre à ce besoin. La plate-forme proposée permet de simuler des charges de travail réalistes sur des bases de données à objets et de mesurer des métriques clés liées aux performances. Elle est constituée de trois composants principaux : un générateur de charges de travail, un injecteur de charges et un collecteur de mesures. Le générateur crée aléatoirement des scénarios d'accès aux données reflétant des cas d'utilisation typiques. L'injecteur soumet ensuite les charges simulées à la base de données cible. Enfin, le collecteur mesure des indicateurs comme le débit, la latence et l'utilisation des ressources au cours des tests. La plate-forme a été testée sur plusieurs bases de données à objets populaires. Les résultats montrent qu'elle permet d'évaluer finement le comportement de ces systèmes sous différents types de sollicitations. En conclusion, cette approche dynamique d'évaluation des performances apporte une solution utile pour comparer les bases de données à objets et identifier leurs points forts et leurs limites.

To address these shortcomings, our methodology employs a generic discrete-event random simulation model parameterized to mimic real-world object access patterns. Database operations are modeled as discrete events scheduled by the simulation executive according to the specified workload. A pluggable cluster model interface allows dropping different clustering algorithms into the simulation for head-to-head comparison. Preliminary results from a proof-of-concept simulator implementing this methodology are presented, demonstrating its ability to accurately measure performance metrics like response time and throughput across adjustments to the mean think time, object access probability distribution and clustering algorithm. This paper addresses this issue by proposing a dynamic object evaluation framework (DOEF) to model changing access patterns. Second, we evaluated two object stores, Platypus and SHORE, exposing Platypus' inferior swapping performance under dynamic access. Overall, DOEF provides a standardized approach for analyzing database systems' responses to shifting access patterns, offering insights to guide optimization as usage evolves over time.

Our study aims to investigate the relationship between SiO maser emission and dust temperature in these stellar environments. Using the Submillimeter Array (SMA) and Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX), we detected SiO maser emission in a diverse range of sources, including asymptotic giant branch stars and red supergiants. Our results suggest a correlation between SiO maser luminosity and dust temperature, providing insights into the physical conditions of the circumstellar envelopes. Overall, our study contributes to the understanding of the role of SiO masers as tracers of the mass-loss process in evolved stars.

title: Deep Spectroscopy of Systematically Surveyed Extended Lyman-alpha  Sources at z~3-5
direct_prompt: Deep Spectroscopy of Systematically Surveyed Extended Lyman-alpha Sources at z~3-5We present deep spectroscopic observations of a sample of 10  extended Lyman-alpha  (Lyman-alpha nebula) sources at z~3-5, selected from narrow-band Subaru imaging survey data with a surface density of 10^-4 arcmin^-2. We obtained the spectra using the Keck/DEIMOS spectrograph to study the physical properties of the sources. The sources have typical extents of ~10-30 kpc and luminosities of ~10^43 erg/s. We find that 60% of the sample show multiple components in their velocity profiles. The velocity offsets between the multiple components are typically a few hundred km/s, but a few have velocity separations of more than 1000 km/s. For these sources with multiple velocity components, we have estimated the dynamical masses to be 10^10-10^11 Msun. We suggest that these are merging systems or clumpy Lyα emitters. The nebular emission lines, such as [OIII]λ5007 and [NII]λ6584, are detected in a few sources. Based on the line ratios of [OIII]/[OII] and [NII]/[OII], we find that the metallicities and ionization parameters of these sources are similar to those of typical Lyman-break galaxies at z~3. The Lyα luminosities of these sources are lower than those of normal galaxies at similar redshifts. This suggests that these extended Lyα sources are powered by a different mechanism, such as shock heating or radiative recombination in the ionized gas.

In this study, we analyze the steep decay phase of the early X-ray afterglows of a sample of GRBs to probe the geometry and dynamics of their jets. Our analysis includes modeling the temporal and spectral evolution of the X-ray afterglows to determine key parameters such as the jet opening angle and bulk Lorentz factor. By comparing our results to theoretical models, we aim to constrain the physical processes at work in GRB jets. The insights gained from this study could have implications for our understanding of the central engine powering GRBs and the mechanisms responsible for their ultra-relativistic jets. Further observations and analyses of X-ray afterglows will be crucial for advancing our knowledge of these enigmatic cosmic events.

title: Fundamental Plane of Sunyaev-Zeldovich clusters
direct_prompt: The Sunyaev-Zeldovich (SZ) effect is a powerful tool for studying the properties of galaxy clusters. The SZ effect causes the cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation to be distorted as it passes through the hot gas surrounding a cluster. By measuring the temperature and polarization of the CMB, we can infer the presence of a cluster and even measure its mass. However, the SZ effect is not a direct measure of the cluster's mass, but rather a proxy that is calibrated using simulations or observations of nearby clusters.In this paper, we present a new method for calibrating the SZ effect using a fundamental plane of galaxy clusters. The fundamental plane is a tight correlation between the cluster's mass, size, and temperature. By using this plane, we can calibrate the SZ effect and measure the mass of clusters with high accuracy and low scatter. We demonstrate the power of our method using a sample of 50 galaxy clusters from the SZ cluster catalog. Our results show that the fundamental plane provides a robust calibration of the SZ effect, allowing us to measure cluster masses with an uncertainty of less than 10%. We also show that our method is less susceptible to systematic errors than traditional calibration methods.Our work provides a significant improvement in the accuracy and precision of SZ-based cluster mass measurements. This will enable better constraints on cosmological models and cluster formation theories. Moreover, our method can be easily applied to future SZ surveys, such as the CMB-S4, which will provide an order of magnitude increase in the number of detected clusters. The fundamental plane of galaxy clusters offers a promising avenue for precision cosmology with SZ surveys.

One promising method to detect and study this gas is through the ne VII hyperfine line at 5755 Angstroms. This line is expected to be bright and relatively free from contamination in million-degree gas, but it is also very weak and requires careful observations. In this paper, we present the results of a deep search for the N VII hyperfine line in a sample of 10 nearby galaxies using the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph on the Hubble Space Telescope. We do not detect the line in any of our galaxies, but we set stringent upper limits on the strength of the line and the amount of million-degree gas in these galaxies. Our results suggest that the incidence of million-degree gas in nearby galaxies may be lower than previously thought, or that the gas may be more clumpy and difficult to detect.

We compare the observed properties of the N VII HFL with the predictions of photoionization and collisional ionization equilibrium (CIE) models. We find that the line emission is well reproduced by CIE models with log(xi) ~ 3.8-4.5, suggesting that the N VII HFL traces the presence of hot (kT ~ 10^6.5-10^7 K) gas with moderate overionization (xi/kT ~ 10^-2-10^-3). Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings for the thermal structure of AGN plasmas.

This paper constructs new examples of type ${\rm II_1}$ factors with prescribed countable fundamental group. Specifically, the fundamental group is constructed as any countable subgroup of the positive real numbers under multiplication. Prior work showed the fundamental group of the hyperfinite ${\rm II_1}$ factor is the whole positive reals, but it was not known if other countable groups could arise. The construction employs asymptotic commuting sequences of unitaries coupled with techniques from deformation/rigidity theory of von Neumann algebras. Properties of the fundamental group are explored, showing it behaves as expected based on previous work. This provides new families of ${\rm II_1}$ factors distinct from existing examples such as group factors. The results add to understanding of classification challenges for ${\rm II_1}$ factors based on their non-uniqueness and flexibility in possible fundamental group structures. Overall, the work expands the known landscape of ${\rm II_1}$ factors.

Applications to constructing subfactors and computing Jones indices are discussed. title: On monotonicity, stability, and construction of central schemes for  hyperbolic conservation laws with source terms (Revised Version)
direct_prompt: **Abstract**In this paper, we propose several improvements to a recent paper of ours in SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis, volume 54, number 4, pages 2032–2053 (2016) on the construction of central schemes for  hyperbolic conservation laws with source terms. The first improvement is the extension of our construction to the multi-dimensional case. This extension is far from straightforward because of the appearance of the commutator between the spatial derivatives and the source term. We prove that this commutator can be controlled in terms of the spatial derivatives of the numerical fluxes, and present an estimate to ensure the stability of the resulting schemes. The second improvement is that our construction of central schemes can be used for general systems of conservation laws. We prove that under suitable assumptions on the source term, the resulting schemes are also stable. The last improvement is the extension of our construction to the case of nonlinear source terms. In this case, we introduce a class of approximate Riemann solvers that enjoy a property we call “strong HLL property”. The schemes based on these approximate Riemann solvers are shown to be stable. Numerical experiments are presented to show the efficiency and robustness of the proposed schemes.

These models can be constrained by interstellar and in situ data, such as the abundance of interstellar neutral helium observed by spacecraft like Voyager. Constraining the models with observational data helps improve our understanding of the physical processes at play in the heliosphere. In this study, we investigate the boundary conditions of the heliosphere using photoionization models and available data sets. We analyze how different assumptions about the interstellar medium and solar radiation affect the predicted properties of the heliospheric boundary. Our results show that accurate constraints on the heliospheric boundary can be obtained by combining interstellar observations with in situ measurements. This approach allows us to refine our understanding of the heliospheric boundary and provide valuable insights into the dynamics of the Sun's interaction with the surrounding interstellar medium. Additionally, our findings have implications for studies of cosmic ray modulation and the transport of interstellar dust particles through the heliosphere. Overall, this research highlights the importance of incorporating observational data into models of the heliosphere to improve our understanding of its boundary conditions.

title: Galaxy clustering constraints on deviations from Newtonian gravity at  cosmological scales II: Perturbative and numerical analyses of power spectrum  and bispectrum
direct_prompt: Galaxy clustering probes the growth rate of cosmic structures and thus is a sensitive tool to constrain deviations from General Relativity (GR). In this paper, we consider the cosmological effects of a specific class of scalar-tensor theories of gravity, Horndeski theories. We focus on a subclass with two free functions, alpha_B and alpha_T, and calculate corrections to the matter power spectrum and bispectrum. By comparing with numerical simulations, we show that perturbation theory provides a reliable description of the non-linear regime, which is important for upcoming galaxy surveys. Using the halo model, we forecast the constraints on alpha_B and alpha_T from future galaxy surveys. In the case of Euclid-like surveys, the combination of cosmic shear and galaxy clustering can reduce the current constraints by a factor of 2-3.
prompt_few_shot: Galaxy clustering constitutes a sensitive probe of gravity on cosmological scales. We consider the power spectrum and the reduced bispectrum in a perturbative framework up to first order in the non-Newtonian parameter beta_1, and compare these results with N-body simulations, whose simulations were ran with the same modifications to gravity. On large scales, we observe a very good agreement between the theoretical calculations and the measurement from simulations. On mildly non-linear scales, the perturbative predictions start to depart from the measurements, which is attributed to non-linear effects that become important at this level. We observe a remarkable cancellation between contributions to the reduced bispectrum arising from the modification of the gravitational interaction and the modification of the growth rate. We also discuss the possibility to constrain beta_1 via the measurement of the galaxy power spectrum and bispectrum from upcoming surveys.

title: Recovering galaxy star formation and metallicity histories from spectra  using VESPA
direct_prompt: In this study, we present a novel approach for recovering galaxy star formation and metallicity histories from spectra using the VESPA code. VESPA is a versatile tool that combines stellar population synthesis models with Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods to infer the star formation and chemical enrichment histories of galaxies. We apply VESPA to a sample of galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey and demonstrate its effectiveness in recovering accurate star formation and metallicity histories. Our results show that VESPA can successfully recover the star formation and metallicity evolution of galaxies over cosmic time. We find that the star formation histories of galaxies are diverse, with some showing continuous star formation while others exhibit bursts of star formation. Additionally, we observe a tight connection between the star formation and metallicity histories of galaxies, highlighting the importance of both in understanding galaxy evolution. Overall, our study demonstrates the potential of VESPA for revealing the complex interplay between star formation and chemical enrichment in galaxies.

Deep, wide-field observations for thisproject were made in two bands at the one meter Swope and 2.5 meter du Ponttelescope at Las Campanas Observatory. Careful attention in reduction andanalysis was paid to the illumination correction, background subtraction, pointspread function determination, and galaxy subtraction. ICL flux is detected inboth bands in all ten clusters ranging from 7.6 x 10^{10} to 7.0 x 10^{11}h^{-1} solar luminosities in r and 1.4 x 10^{10} to 1.2 x 10^{11} h^{-1} solarluminosities in the B-band. These fluxes account for 6 to 22% of the totalcluster light within one quarter of the virial radius in r and 4 to 21% in theB-band. Average ICL B-r colors range from 1.5 to 2.8 mags when k and evolutioncorrected to the present epoch. In several clusters we also detect ICL in groupenvironments near the cluster center and up to ~1 h^{-1} Mpc distant from thecluster center. Our sample, having been selected from the Abell sample, isincomplete in that it does not include high redshift clusters with low density,low flux, or low mass, and it does not include low redshift clusters with highflux, mass, or density. This bias makes it difficult to interpret correlationsbetween ICL flux and cluster properties. Despite this selection bias, we dofind that the presence of a cD galaxy corresponds to both centrallyconcentrated galaxy profiles and centrally concentrated ICL profiles. This isconsistent with ICL either forming from galaxy interactions at the center, orforming at earlier times in groups and later combining in the center.

title: The Kalman--Yakubovich--Popov inequality for passive discrete  time-invariant systems
direct_prompt: Here is a 6 sentence abstract for the article:Stability and passivity are important properties for control systems. This article investigates passivity conditions for discrete time-invariant systems using the Kalman--Yakubovich--Popov (KYP) inequality. The KYP inequality provides a linear matrix inequality test to check the passivity of a system. The authors formulate a discrete version of the KYP inequality for passive discrete time-invariant systems. It is shown that a system is passive if and only if its transfer function satisfies the proposed discrete KYP inequality. Simulation and experimental results on a physical system demonstrate that the discrete KYP inequality can accurately verify passivity for real-world discrete time systems. This work extends the use of KYP inequalities to provide valuable passivity conditions for the analysis and design of discrete time control systems.

Our results suggest that LBG J2135 is a promising lens system for studying dark matter substructures.

title: Search for Direct Photons from $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200GeV$ AuAu Collisions  Using a New $\pi^{0}$ Tagging Method in the PHENIX Experiment at RHIC
direct_prompt: **Abstract**We report the first measurement of direct photons from Au+Au collisions at \(\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200\text{ GeV}\) using a new method to tag neutral pions (\(\pi^0\)). The measurement is based on the analysis of data collected by the PHENIX experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). The new tagging method uses the PHENIX electromagnetic calorimeter (EMCal) to identify \(\pi^0\)s via their two-photon decay mode. This method provides a significant improvement in the signal-to-background ratio compared to previous methods. The measured direct photon yield is consistent with the predictions of perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) calculations. This measurement provides new insights into the production of direct photons in heavy ion collisions and constrains the gluon distribution in the nuclear wave function.
prompt_few_shot: Direct photons are a powerful probe to study the matter created in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions. Direct photons are emitted from all stages of the collision and once produced, they leave the interaction region without further modification by the medium. The PHENIX experiment at RHIC has measured direct photon production in Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV in transverse momentum ($p_T$) range from 0 to 20 GeV/$c$. A new method using $\pi^0$ tagging is employed to improve the low $p_T$ reach down to 0.5 GeV/$c$. The measured $p_T$ spectrum is compared to perturbative quantum chromodynamics calculations, and the nuclear modification factor ($R_{AA}$) is presented. The results are compared to other measurements and to model calculations.

direct_prompt: X-ray emissions from two-temperature accretion flows within a dipole magnetic funnelAbstract:Accretion flows onto neutron stars are often associated with strong magnetic fields, and the accretion columns are likely to be channeled by the magnetic fields to form a funnel-like structure. We find that the thermal bremsstrahlung emission from the accreting matter and the synchrotron emission from the secondary pairs dominate the spectra. The radiation pressure plays an important role in the accretion dynamics. Our calculations show that, under some conditions, the radiation force can significantly reduce the accretion luminosity and even blow away the accretion flow, leading to an effective suppression of the radiation. The dependences of the spectral and timing properties on the viewing angle and the magnetic field strength are investigated. The comparisons with the typical properties of several X-ray sources suggest that our model can be applied to some observed sources.

Positronium is the bound state between an electron and its antimatter counterpart, a positron. Currently, nonrelativistic approximations are commonly used to model positronium states. However, these approximations break down at small distances and high momenta where relativistic effects become significant. The authors develop a relativistic Schrodinger equation to describe positronium without relying on nonrelativistic approximations. Through analytical and numerical methods, they compute the ground state energy and wavefunction of positronium using this relativistic theory. The results provide more accurate modeling of positronium compared to existing nonrelativistic approximations, demonstrating the importance of relativistic effects for positronium spectroscopy.

Through numerical simulation and perturbation methods, we track the bifurcating fixed points and characterize the phase space in the neighborhood of the bifurcation. The results provide insights into the dynamics and stability of realistic physical systems exhibiting transcritical bifurcations.

The results show that the topological entropy remains quantized above low temperatures, demonstrating that topological order persists up to appreciable energy scales. However, the entropy slowly decreases with increasing temperature as thermal fluctuations generate more anyonic quasiparticle pairs. A phase transition into a topologically trivial phase is found to occur at a nonzero critical temperature. Additionally, the entanglement properties of the code are studied through various bipartite entanglement measures. Overall, this work provides a comprehensive characterization of the thermal stability of topological order in the toric code.

title: A case for variational geomagnetic data assimilation: insights from a  one-dimensional, nonlinear, and sparsely observed MHD system

This setup is designed to mimic critical aspects of the geomagnetic field's behavior. The findings underscore the utility of variational geomagnetic data assimilation, especially in scenarios with limited and noisy observations. The study highlights the benefits of this approach and paves the way for further exploration and implementation in more complex and realistic settings.

title: Flow instabilities of magnetic flux tubes II. Longitudinal flow
direct_prompt: Here is an 8 sentence abstract for the article title "Flow instabilities of magnetic flux tubes II. Longitudinal flow":Magnetohydrodynamic simulations have greatly improved our understanding of longitudinal flows along magnetic flux tubes in the solar atmosphere. However, the stability properties of these flows remain an important open problem. In this work, we build upon previous investigations of flux tube flow instabilities by considering the effects of longitudinal flow profiles. Using a linear perturbation analysis, we derive analytical criteria for the onset of different instability modes driven by longitudinal flows along thin magnetic flux tubes. We find that longitudinal flows can drive kink-type, sausage-type, and higherorder instability modes depending on the flow profile and plasma beta values. Comparisons with full nonlinear simulations show good agreement regarding instability growth rates and saturation amplitudes. Our results have implications for dynamic phenomena in solar prominences, spicules, and other structured features involving longitudinal flows along magnetic flux lines. Further investigation is still needed to incorporate more realistic physics such as non-ideal MHD effects and magnetic field diffusivity.
prompt_few_shot: Here is an 8 sentence academic article abstract for the given title:We investigate the effects of longitudinal flows on the stability and dynamics of magnetic flux tubes located near the base of the solar convection zone. Using nonlinear numerical simulations, we examine thin magnetic flux tubes subject to flows parallel to the magnetic field lines. We determine the parameter ranges for longitudinal flow speed and duration that allow magnetic flux to be stored in the overshoot region for time periods comparable to the solar dynamo cycle. The numerical simulations are compared with simplified analytical approximations. It is found that longitudinal downflows of up to 50 m/s persisting for less than 100 days can store a magnetic flux tube of 2x10^21 Mx in the overshoot layer for the multi-year dynamo cycle. Faster or longer longitudinal flows are found to advect the flux tube out of the overshoot region too rapidly. The implications of these results for the storage and emergence of solar magnetic fields are discussed.

title: A new Generation of Spectrometer Calibration Techniques based on Optical  Frequency Combs
direct_prompt: Here is an 11 sentence abstract for the article title provided:Advances in optical frequency comb technology have enabled new high-precision techniques for spectrometer calibration. Optical frequency combs provide a series of precisely spaced electromagnetic frequencies that can be used to map out individual spectral elements in an instrument. In this paper, we introduce a new method for spectrometer calibration that leverages recent developments in broad and widely tunable optical frequency combs. Our technique utilizes a supercontinuum fiber laser to generate an optical frequency comb source spanning the full wavelength range of a high-resolution spectrometer. We describe the implementation of our calibration scheme and present a detailed analysis of its accuracy and precision. The results demonstrate sub-picometer wavelength accuracy and parts-per-billion frequency reproducibility across the full detection band. This new approach allows for rapid, robust and traceable calibration of modern broad-bandwidth spectrometers. Spectrometer calibration is a crucial step in many areas of science and this novel technique offers significant advantages over existing methods. We discuss how our combbased calibration scheme could enable new applications for high-resolution spectroscopy. Overall, this work establishes a new generation of optical frequency comb-based calibration techniques well-suited to next-generation broad-bandwidth spectrometers.

direct_prompt: Atomic electric dipole moments (EDMs) are permanent asymmetric distributions of electric charge within an atom or molecule. In this work, we review the fundamental theorem of Schiff, which constrains the values of these EDMs for stationary states of atoms and molecules. These corrections include contributions from hadronic and nuclear sources, as well as effects due to the finite size of the nucleus. We also discuss the connection between EDMs and fundamental symmetries, such as parity and time-reversal invariance. Finally, we briefly outline the current experimental status of EDM searches and future prospects in this field.

The SBF method is a perturbative approach that treats the nucleus as a small perturbation to the atomic Hamiltonian. The FW method is a non-perturbative approach that uses a unitary transformation to remove the center-of-mass motion of the nucleus. title: Spectroscopic Observations of the Intermediate Polar EX Hydrae in  Quiescence
direct_prompt: In this study, we present the results of spectroscopic observations of the intermediate polar EX Hydrae in quiescence. The observations were obtained using the 6.5m Magellan Clay Telescope at the Las Campanas Observatory in Chile. We analyzed the spectra of EX Hydrae to study the behavior of the accretion disk and white dwarf in this binary system. Our spectroscopic observations reveal the presence of prominent emission lines, which are indicative of accretion activity in the system. The H-alpha line shows a broad component, suggesting the presence of an accretion disk in the system. We also detect strong emission lines of He I, indicating the presence of a white dwarf in the binary system. The analysis of the spectra allows us to estimate the mass accretion rate onto the white dwarf in EX Hydrae. Our results provide valuable insights into the accretion processes in intermediate polars during quiescence. The spectroscopic observations of EX Hydrae in quiescence contribute to our understanding of the mass transfer mechanisms in close binary systems. Overall, our study highlights the importance of spectroscopic observations in studying the properties of intermediate polars in different states.

Spin-modulated radialvelocities consistent with an outer disc origin were detected for the firsttime in an IP. The spin pulsation was modulated with velocities near ~500-600km/s. These velocities are consistent with those of material circulating at theouter edge of the accretion disc, suggesting corotation of the accretioncurtain with material near the Roche lobe radius. These findings have confirmed thetheoretical model predictions of King & Wynn (1999), Belle et al. (2002) andNorton et al. (2004) for EX Hya, which predict large accretion curtains thatextend to a distance close to the Roche lobe radius in this system. Evidencefor overflow stream of material falling onto the magnetosphere was observed,confirming the result of Belle et al. (2005) that disc overflow in EX Hya ispresent during quiescence as well as outburst. It appears that the hbeta andhgamma spin radial velocities originated from the rotation of the funnel at theouter disc edge, while those of halpha were produced due to the flow ofmaterial along the field lines far from the white dwarf (narrow component) andclose to the white dwarf (broad-base component), in agreement with theaccretion curtain model.

Both the low-temperature and high-temperature approximations show very good agreement with simulations in their respective regimes of validity. The approximations also compare well with results from standard integral equation closures such as the Percus-Yevick and hypernetted chain theories, providing an accurate but computationally inexpensive description of penetrable-sphere fluids.

We conclude that the evidence for a universal IMF is inconclusive, and that more research is needed to resolve this issue.

Using state-of-the-art population synthesis models and adopting different IMFs, we compare model predictions to the observed CIL colors. We show that a universal IMF can adequately fit the colors of early-type galaxies, disfavoring scenarios requiring a variable IMF. Our analysis demonstrates that using a single stellar population model we can constrain the shape of the IMF and shows the power of color measurements to derive fundamental properties of galaxies in the local and distant Universe.

title: Particle-vibration coupling within covariant density functional theory
direct_prompt: Here is a 9 sentence abstract for the provided article title:The coupling between nuclear collective motion and individual nucleonic degrees of freedom, known as particle-vibration coupling (PVC), is an important nuclear structure effect that needs to be properly accounted for in theoretical nuclear structure models. In this article, we explore a microscopic treatment of PVC within the framework of covariant density functional theory (CDFT). We derive and implement an exact particle-phonon coupling formalism based on a single-particle representation of the nuclear collective vibrations computed with the quasiparticle random phase approximation on top of CDFT mean-field states. We present results for PVC corrections to single-particle energies throughout the nuclear chart and investigate their isotopic dependence. The impact of PVC on nuclear properties like binding energies, radii, and low-lying excitations is analyzed. We find non-negligible PVC contributions that help restore spin-orbit splittings and shell closures modified by CDFT mean-field dynamics. Overall, this work establishes a fully self-consistent framework to incorporate dynamical correlations beyond the mean-field in covariant energy density functionals.

The method is formulated in terms of the Bethe-Salpeter equation in the two-quasiparticle space with an energy-dependent two-quasiparticle residual interaction. We propose a novel quantization scheme for the precoding matrix that takes into account the channel conditions and system constraints. Through simulation studies, we demonstrate the benefits of the proposed quantization scheme in terms of capacity improvement and performance optimization. Our results show that by carefully designing the quantization process, the system capacity can be significantly increased compared to traditional precoding methods. We also analyze the impact of channel conditions, such as coherence time and antenna spacing, on the capacity performance. Additionally, we investigate the influence of different quantization levels on the system capacity and provide insights into selecting an optimal quantization strategy for maximizing capacity. Overall, our study sheds light on the importance of quantized precoding in enhancing the capacity of multiple-antenna fading channels.

title: A deeper X-ray study of the core of the Perseus galaxy cluster: the  power of sound waves and the distribution of metals and cosmic rays
direct_prompt: Abstract:This paper is focused on the results obtained through an X-ray deeper observation of the core of the Perseus galaxy cluster with the aim to investigate the role played by sound waves in the physics of the intracluster medium (ICM). The X-ray analysis was performed exploiting the high-resolution X-ray spectra provided by the Reflection Grating Spectrometer (RGS) on board XMM-Newton. We measured the temperature, the density, the metallicity, and the abundance of O, Ne, Si, S, Ar, Ca, and Fe in the core of the cluster. In addition, by analyzing the line broadening of the emission lines we provided a measure of the bulk gas motions and an estimate of the turbulent pressure. The analysis of the metal distribution and of the temperature allowed us to derive the metallicity gradient and the entropy profile in the central region of the cluster. We measured a metallicity gradient steeper than that observed in other clusters and we found evidence of a drop in the entropy in the core. These findings suggest that the Perseus cluster could be in a cooling phase and that sound waves are an efficient mechanism for transporting energy.
prompt_few_shot: The Perseus galaxy cluster is the brightest galaxy cluster in the X-ray band. It is an ideal laboratory to study the complex interplay between multiple physical processes in the intra-cluster medium (ICM), which is the hot (T~10^7-10^8 K) plasma that permeates galaxy clusters. We present a detailed X-ray analysis of a 300 ks Chandra observation of the Perseus cluster core, which allowed us to derive the temperature, density, and pressure profiles out to ~100 kpc from the cluster center. We found that sound waves play a major role in regulating the thermodynamics of the ICM in the cool-core of the Perseus cluster, while thermal conduction is inefficient. The metal abundances in the ICM show an outward gradient, with a drop of about 50% in the central 100 kpc. We also found evidence for the presence of cosmic rays in the ICM, which may be reaccelerated by turbulence driven by the sound waves.

title: SuprimeCam Observation of Sporadic Meteors during Perseids 2004
direct_prompt: Here is a 10 sentence abstract for the article:The Perseids meteor shower occurs annually in mid-August and often produces the most meteor activity of the year. This study utilized observations taken by the Subaru Prime Focus Camera (SuprimeCam) on the nights of August 11-13, 2004 to observe meteors during the peak of the Perseids that year. Over the course of three nights, the wide field of view camera captured video footage equivalent to over 100 hours and recorded 107 meteor trails. The meteor magnitudes, velocities, and trajectories were measured and analyzed from the SuprimeCam data. Preliminary results found the measured velocities to be consistent with previous Perseids studies, with most meteors traveling between 30-60 km/s. The study is one of the first to use a wide-field camera to conduct a survey of sporadic meteors concurrently with a meteor shower. Future work will refine the orbit analysis to distinguish between Perseids and non-Perseids meteors observed. It is hoped this research can help increase our understanding of the meteoroid streams that produce the Perseids shower and the relationship between shower and non-shower meteors observed on the same nights.
